title: Differential kernel gating + prefill-aware scheduling for mixed-length workloads
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a differential kernel gating layer and a prefill-aware scheduling policy that jointly pick kernels per-request based on hardware fingerprint and sequence-length distribution. Goal is to reduce p95 latency for mixed prefill/decode traffic while lowering per-token cost at tail. This ticket contains design, experiment plan, implementation and rollout guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: New gating component can select between at least three candidate kernels per model (fast-prefill, balanced, low-memory) using lightweight features within 200us decision time
End-to-end prefill+decode pipeline shows >=8% p95 latency reduction on dialog-bench-v2 when toggled to seqlen-aware policy versus current static kernel policy
No regression on p50 latency or token throughput (<=1% change) across completion-load-50k synthetic workload
Integration tests cover fallback path: if kernel fails or OOMs, runtime transparently retries with alternative kernel within SLO boundaries
Playbook for bumping canary and rollback is documentated and validated with a dry run
benchmarks: dialog-bench-v2: mixed 30% long-prefill / 70% short-prefill, baseline p95=280ms, target p95<=258ms
completion-load-50k: uniform seq-len 128, baseline tokens/sec=8200, target throughput within 1%
memory-safety: peak GPU memory headroom >8% on A100-40G when using low-memory kernel
progress_updates: 2026-02-24: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and perf teams. Consensus to prototype gating as a lightweight decision function in C++ runtime layer.
2026-03-02: Prototype merged for local testing (PR 1452). Initial microbench shows decision overhead ~120us on x86 control path.
2026-03-07: Experiment harness prepared: canary pool created with dedicated-tag 'gating-canary'. Synthetic load scripts pushed to perf infra.
2026-03-12: Early A/B run indicates p95 improvement on dialog-bench-v2 of ~6.1% with default thresholds; tuning scheduled.
2026-03-14: Tuned gating thresholds and added warm-start fingerprint for kernels. Observed 8.7% p95 improvement in second A/B run; preparing rollout playbook.
implementation_notes: Decision features: model_id, request_prefill_len, avg_decode_len, last-seen-prefill-bucket, gpu_arch_fingerprint
Gating model: simple rule tree with annealing parameters for exploration during canary (epsilon-greedy bandit-like behavior)
Prefill scheduler: groups requests into short/long microbatches and routes short-prefill batches to low-latency kernel while long-prefill batches use high-throughput kernel
Safety nets: kernel fallback path triggers when runtime error or when measured latency exceeds per-request budget for 3 consecutive requests
Observability: emit decision_id, chosen_kernel, reason_code, decision_latency, and per-request kernel metrics to tracing pipeline
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Decision overhead adds tail latency for tiny decode-only requests. Mitigation: bypass gating for requests with decode-only flag and pre-configured microbatch size <=2.
Risk: Exploration may choose suboptimal kernel under hot reconfiguration. Mitigation: constrain exploration budget and require decay schedule + manual override in console.
Risk: Increased memory fragmentation when switching kernels. Mitigation: add a short cooldown per-GPU and prefer low-memory kernel when headroom <10%
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): deploy gating to 2% of hosted traffic on dedicated-canary pool for 48 hours. Monitor p95/p99, OOMs, and GPU memory headroom.
Stage 2 (gradual): expand to 20% over 3 days if no regressions. Run regression suite nightly.
Stage 3 (release): enable for all Dedicated pools with option flag off for legacy Private deployments. Publish rollout notes and operator controls in Console.
Rollback: immediate switch to static kernel policy via feature flag if p99 increases by >10% or any OOM spike detected
test_plan: Unit tests for gating decision function and histogram bucketing
Integration tests simulating kernel fallback and verifying memory safety
Perf regression tests comparing baseline vs gating on dialog-bench-v2 and completion-load-50k
Chaos tests: simulated kernel crash and network blips to ensure graceful degrade
notes_for_reviewers: Please review gating thresholds in runtime/config/gating_defaults.yaml. We're intentionally conservative for initial canary.
Pay attention to the new telemetry keys for cost attribution. Finance wants token-level cost mapping to chosen kernels.
Design doc includes a short decision tree that must be translated to fast C++ path; prefer no std::map allocations on the fast path
